reports.title: Liquidia Corporation Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

lines: Under the settlement agreement, Liquidia agreed to pay net $380.7 million in multiple installments in 2026 and 2027, inclusive of payments to other parties to resolve the antitrust litigation against United Therapeutics related to Treprostinil Injection, which the company expects to fund from current cash and cash equivalents and ongoing sales of YUTREPIA.

desk.headline: Revenue up to $225.3m as YUTREPIA sales rose 31% q/q; $389.7m legal settlement charge drove a $236.3m net loss; no financial guidance

other.label: Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP)
other.change: up from $96.3m in Q2; fifth straight rise

other.label: Cash and cash equivalents
other.change: up from $190.7m at end-2025, before settlement payments

results: Total revenue was $225.3m against $54.3m a year earlier, as YUTREPIA (inhaled treprostinil, launched mid-2025) sold $222.7m, up 31% on Q2.
A $389.7m charge for the global settlement with United Therapeutics turned the quarter into a $236.3m net loss ($2.64 per share).
Excluding that charge and share pay, adjusted EBITDA rose for a fifth quarter to $140.5m; R&D rose to $25.3m and SG&A to $59.0m.
Cash reached $396.1m at end-September; the company owes a net $380.7m in instalments over 2026–27 and plans to pay from cash and ongoing sales.
Under the deal YUTREPIA stays on sale for PAH, but the PH-ILD indication is being removed from its label and promotion there has stopped.

guidance.summary: Liquidia gives no revenue or earnings guidance. It gave study timelines instead: SPRINT to start in Q4 2026, RE-WARM (Raynaud's) primary completion in Q1 2027 and L606 pivotal studies running into 2029.

points: The CEO said doctors value the control and flexibility YUTREPIA gives over each patient's dosing, and demand has held up.
October patient shipments were the highest monthly level since launch, and October added more first-time prescribers than September.
With the litigation resolved, the focus shifts to Phase 4 studies in PAH to build YUTREPIA's case as a first-choice prostacyclin.
Pipeline: L606 pivotal trials in PH-ILD and PAH, a planned PH-COPD study from H2 2027, and FDA Fast Track for YUTREPIA in SSc-RP.
call.source: CEO comments in the results release (Exhibit 99.1) and the results presentation (Exhibit 99.2); no independent call transcript found
